column1: # ADR-0056 D10 B12 / V98 (amendment 19, A4e-6): the golden of the digest of a scope.
# Go runs it (internal/edition, scopedigest_test.go). This table is plain ASCII,
# TAB-separated, no quoting.
# A row is   case<TAB>digest<TAB>ids<TAB>input
#   case    a name for the row.
#   ids     the ids of the scope, in its order, separated by commas (an id is in the
#           grammar of challengeid.Pattern: it holds no comma and no LF). They are
#           synthetic ids of that grammar, not challenges of the repository.
#   input   the exact bytes the digest is the sha256 of, spelled for printf: \n is LF,
#           nothing else is escaped. The bytes are the label falco-ctf/edition/scope/v1,
#           one LF, and then every id of the scope in its order, each followed by one LF.
#   digest  lower-case hex of the sha256 of those bytes. It is NOT copied from the output
#           of the code under test: it is computed from the input column alone, with
#           printf '<input column>' | shasum -a 256
#           (the input holds no percent sign, so the column is a safe printf format).
# The test reads the table three ways: the digest column is the sha256 of the input
# column; the input column is what the definition makes of the ids; and
# edition.ScopeDigest of the ids is the digest column.
one
two
two-swapped
